claim: ADHD is a heterogeneous neuropsychiatric disorder highly prevalent in children, characterized by impairments in attention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity.
source: Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a heterogeneous neuropsychiatric disorder highly prevalent in children, characterized by impairments in attention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity (Faraone et al., 2015; Tsai, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Faraone et al., 2015; Tsai, 2017).

claim: Psychostimulants such as amphetamine and methylphenidate are recommended as first-line pharmacological therapy for patients with ADHD.
source: Psychostimulants, such as amphetamine and methylphenidate (MPH) that work by increasing central dopamine and norepinephrine activity in the brain, are recommended as first-line pharmacological therapy for patients with ADHD (Faraone, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Faraone, 2018).

claim: Psychostimulants work by increasing central dopamine and norepinephrine activity in the brain.
source: Psychostimulants, such as amphetamine and methylphenidate (MPH) that work by increasing central dopamine and norepinephrine activity in the brain, are recommended as first-line pharmacological therapy for patients with ADHD (Faraone, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Faraone, 2018).

claim: Some ADHD patients fail to respond to psychostimulants or experience adverse effects including cardiovascular effects.
source: Although these drugs impact executive and attentional functions, some patients fail to respond or experience adverse effects including cardiovascular effects, and discontinue the treatment (Faraone, 2018; Tsai, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Faraone, 2018; Tsai, 2017).

claim: Genetic factors play a significant role in the development of ADHD.
source: The pathogenesis of ADHD is not fully understood, but genetic factors play a significant role in its development (Kent, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Kent, 2004).

claim: Most therapeutic candidates for ADHD have focused on modulating the dopaminergic neurotransmission system.
source: Most therapeutic candidates have focused on modulating the dopaminergic neurotransmission system, with additional candidates involving the noradrenergic and serotonergic systems (Banaschewski et al., 2010; Kent, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Banaschewski et al., 2010; Kent, 2004).

claim: Dopamine plays an important role in behavioral processes such as cognition and emotional processing.
source: In particular, the neurotransmitter dopamine plays an important role in behavioral processes such as cognition and emotional processing; therefore, its dysfunction is involved in several neuropsychiatric disorders including ADHD (Faraone and Biederman, 1998; Leo et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Faraone and Biederman, 1998; Leo et al., 2018).

claim: Dopamine dysfunction is involved in several neuropsychiatric disorders including ADHD.
source: In particular, the neurotransmitter dopamine plays an important role in behavioral processes such as cognition and emotional processing; therefore, its dysfunction is involved in several neuropsychiatric disorders including ADHD (Faraone and Biederman, 1998; Leo et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Faraone and Biederman, 1998; Leo et al., 2018).

claim: Alterations in dopaminergic neurotransmission within the mesocorticolimbic system are involved in the pathophysiology of ADHD.
source: Alterations in dopaminergic neurotransmission within the mesocorticolimbic system are involved in the pathophysiology of ADHD, with functional abnormalities in fronto-basal ganglia networks (Biederman and Faraone, 2002; Hart et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Biederman and Faraone, 2002; Hart et al., 2013).

claim: Genes associated with neuronal development and plasticity are considered important targets in the clinical manifestation and pathogenesis of ADHD.
source: Genes associated with neuronal development and plasticity are considered another important target in the clinical manifestation and pathogenesis of ADHD (Banaschewski et al., 2010; Galvez-Contreras et al., 2017; Tsai, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Banaschewski et al., 2010; Galvez-Contreras et al., 2017; Tsai, 2017).

claim: Neurotrophic factors are essential for neural development of the brain and plasticity in adults and are involved in the pathogenesis of ADHD.
source: Neurotrophic factors (NTFs) are essential for neural development of the brain and plasticity in adults and are involved in the pathogenesis of ADHD (Bilgiç et al., 2017; Tsai, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Bilgiç et al., 2017; Tsai, 2017).

claim: BDNF has been identified in the pathophysiology of ADHD and represents a biological target for treatments of this disorder.
source: In particular, brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) has been identified in the pathophysiology of ADHD and represents a biological target for treatments of this disorder (Conner et al., 2008; Kent et al., 2005; Tsai, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Conner et al., 2008; Kent et al., 2005; Tsai, 2017).

claim: tDCS has been extensively investigated in children with a variety of diagnoses, including neuropsychiatric disorders, and has shown no serious adverse effects.
source: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has been extensively investigated in children with a variety of diagnoses, including neuropsychiatric disorders, and has shown no serious adverse effects (Bikson et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Bikson et al., 2016).

claim: tDCS improves short- and long-term memory deficits in an ADHD animal model.
source: tDCS improves short- and long-term memory deficits and is associated with altered dopamine levels and enhanced synaptic activity, respectively, as shown in an ADHD animal model (Leffa et al., 2018; Leffa et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Leffa et al., 2018; Leffa et al., 2016).

claim: tDCS is associated with altered dopamine levels and enhanced synaptic activity in an ADHD animal model.
source: tDCS improves short- and long-term memory deficits and is associated with altered dopamine levels and enhanced synaptic activity, respectively, as shown in an ADHD animal model (Leffa et al., 2018; Leffa et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Leffa et al., 2018; Leffa et al., 2016).

claim: Anodal tDCS exerts beneficial effects on higher order cognitive functions such as working memory, attention, and perception in patients with diabetes and animal models.
source: Anodal tDCS exerts beneficial effects on higher order cognitive functions, such as working memory, attention, and perception, in patients with diabetes and animal models through the augmentation of synaptic plasticity, thus requiring BDNF secretion (Coffman et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Coffman et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2017).

claim: Anodal tDCS effects on cognitive functions occur through the augmentation of synaptic plasticity, requiring BDNF secretion.
source: Anodal tDCS exerts beneficial effects on higher order cognitive functions, such as working memory, attention, and perception, in patients with diabetes and animal models through the augmentation of synaptic plasticity, thus requiring BDNF secretion (Coffman et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Coffman et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2017).

claim: ADHD has comorbid cognitive dysfunction disorders.
source: Because ADHD has comorbid cognitive dysfunction disorders (Faraone et al., 2015; Tsai, 2017), tDCS has been proposed as a possible therapeutic option for treating patients with ADHD (Leffa et al., 2018; Leffa et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Faraone et al., 2015; Tsai, 2017).

claim: tDCS has been proposed as a possible therapeutic option for treating patients with ADHD.

claim: Conventional tDCS using saline sponge-based rectangular pads stimulates a large scalp area and the current flow is not concentrated on targeted neuronal populations.

claim: HD-tDCS treatment alleviated cognitive deficits in SHR rats.
source: This treatment alleviated cognitive deficits, with an increase in tyrosine hydroxylase and vesicular monoamine transporter two and significantly decreased plasma membrane reuptake transporter (DAT).

claim: In the open-field test, SHR and sham animals showed significant hyperactivity compared to the WKY group.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the study and Figure 1A.

evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental data from the study, supported by citations to published literature (Antal et al., 2017; Jackson et al., 2016; Liebetanz et al., 2009).

claim: Anodal HD-tDCS application offers a potential adjuvant therapy for psychiatric disorders such as ADHD and may improve recovery of cognitive dysfunctions.
source: In summary anodal HD-tDCS application offers a potential adjuvant therapy for psychiatric disorders such as ADHD and may improve recovery of cognitive dysfunctions.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental data from the study.

claim: The predicted peak electric field intensity was 2.4 V/m in the frontal cortex.
source: Anodal stimulation was delivered at an intensity of 63.7 A/m2 over the prefrontal cortex. The predicted peak electric field intensity was 2.4 V/m in the frontal cortex.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling data from the study and Figure 6A.

claim: The predicted peak current density was 2.1 A/m2 in the prefrontal cortex.
source: The predicted peak current densities were 2.1 A/m2 and 3.3 A/m2 in the prefrontal cortex and primary motor cortex, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling data from the study.

claim: The predicted peak electric field intensity over the primary motor cortex was 3.5 V/m.
source: The predicted peak electric field intensity was 2.4 V/m in the prefrontal cortex and 3.5 V/m in the primary motor cortex.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling data from the study.

claim: The predicted peak current density over the primary motor cortex was 3.3 A/m2.
source: The predicted peak current densities were 2.1 A/m2 and 3.3 A/m2 in the prefrontal cortex and primary motor cortex, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational modeling data from the study.
